No, companies do not have to accept cash. The law about money is that it's a legal tender for debts. A transaction at a store requires the store to agree to said transaction. In other words, if you don't pay in cash then they simply don't agree to the transaction. You can't claim they're not accepting your legal tender for your debt, since you have no debt with the store's agreement.

edit Like others mentioned though, if you already have an agreed upon debt like when you eat a restaurant before paying then they would be unable to refuse cash as it is legal tender for any debt - and you now have a debt.
